newsitem.title: USA: CMS Energy plans joint venture with Ghana.
newsitem.headline: CMS Energy plans joint venture with Ghana.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp said its independent power unit, CMS Generation Co, has formed a joint venture with the Republic of Ghana's Volta River Authority (VRA) to develop and manage a series of energy infrastructure projects in Ghana and the West African region.

CMS said its involvement in Ghana is a response to the government's call for private foreign capital to participate in energy development. The joint venture's first project is the acquistion of VRA's Takoradi thermal plant, a 300-megawatt oil- and gas-fueled, combined-cycle electric generating plant under construction at Aboadze, near Takoradi.

CMS said it and VRA are now working to determine the valuation for the Takoradi plant and establish due diligence requirements. The two companies will also negotiate a management services agreement under which the joint venture will manage, operate and maintain the Takoradi plant. The Takoradi plant is scheduled to enter commercial operation in the third quarter of 1997.

The joint venture will also pursue the feasibility of developing the Bui Hydroelectric Plant, a 400-megawatt generating facility which would be built on the Black Volta River in central Ghana. In addition, the agreement contemplates examining the feasibility of other projects including a natural gas pipeline.

"This agreement combines the highly-respected Volta River Authority with CMS Energy, which has the capital, operating and financing experience and technical capability necessary to develop energy projects to serve Ghana's stable and growing economy," CMS Generation President Rodney Boulanger said in a statement.
